text: ENS-GI Digital Twin: A multiscale physics-based computational framework simulating the Enteric Nervous System (ENS) and gastrointestinal motility. Three distinct applications: 1) Research Simulator (biophysical equation-based), 2) Neuromorphic Hardware (SPICE/Verilog-A export), 3) Clinical Predictor (patient-specific parameterization for IBS diagnosis). 10,000+ lines of production Python code, 8 V…

Critical Architecture: Layer 1 - Cellular electrophysiology with extended Hodgkin-Huxley model (Na, K, Ca, KCa, A-type K, Leak channels). Layer 2 - ENS neuron network with gap junctions and chemical synapses. Layer 3 - ICC pacemaker and smooth muscle dynamics. Layer 4 - Clinical AI (PINN, Bayesian, virtual drug trials). All 6 ion channels now properly exported to SPICE (was only 3).

Cannot make clinical claims without real validation. Transfer learning possible with 10-15 real patients + pre-training on 10k synthetic samples.

Simulation Cache Infrastructure (NEW): SimulationCache class for LRU caching of expensive digital twin simulations. Disk-persistent across sessions.

CRITICAL: Simulation uses accelerated timescale (16× faster than biological). ICCParams.omega = 0.005 rad/ms gives ~48 cpm in simulation but represents biological ~3 cpm. Divide all simulation frequencies by 16 for biological equivalents. Motility index is ×100 scaled (24.36 = 0.2436 normalized). Biomarker test ranges are in accelerated units: Healthy ICC: 40-55 cpm, IBS-D: 65-85 cpm, IBS-C: 15-25…

IBS Profile Biomarker Ranges (Accelerated timescale): Healthy ICC: 40-55 cpm (biological ~3 cpm), IBS-D motility: 30-50 (hyperexcitable, +42% vs healthy), IBS-C motility: 10-20 (hypoexcitable, -42% vs healthy), IBS-M: 3-4 cpm ICC. IBS-D mechanism: increased Na+ conductance. IBS-C mechanism: decreased Ca2+ conductance. Motility index formula: mean_contractile_force * 100.

Core Neuron Mathematical Model (Hodgkin-Huxley): C_m * dV/dt = -I_Na - I_K - I_Ca - I_KCa - I_A - I_L + I_ext + I_syn + I_gap. ICC FitzHugh-Nagumo: dv/dt = v - v^3/3 - w, dw/dt = epsilon(v + a - bw). ENS 'second brain': ~100 million neurons, controls GI motility/secretion/blood flow, semi-autonomous from CNS. Parameters: g_Na=120, g_K=36, g_CaL=4, g_KCa=5, g_A=8, g_L=0.3 (all mS/cm2).

PyMC3/Bayesian is completely optional - PINN framework works without it. This is the minimum viable install for development and testing.

OPU feasibility study for Tritone: core hypothesis to test is that optical/analog MVM noise corrupts a PINN's DERIVATIVES (sensitivities) faster than its output VALUES, because the PINN's usefulness depends on d(output)/d(input). Ternary weights are a good optics match (3 levels {-1->0phase,+1->pi-phase,0->blocked}, sparsity=no light path), but bit-exactness (Tritone's crown jewel) is the opposite…

OPU study success metrics: (1) usable-SNR threshold = lowest optical SNR(dB) where ADDED value rel-MAE stays under Tritone's existing 19.4% ternarization budget; (2) derivative-amplification factor = jacobian_rel_mae / value_rel_mae (hypothesis >1); (3) verdict GO/CONDITIONAL/NO-GO. Out of scope: photonic layout, training-through-optics, real .keras weights (hook only), energy/area.
